message.subject: Letters from the site no. 31: mud, mostly
message.body:
Dear reader,

It rained for four days straight and my site turned into a paddling pool. I spent Tuesday in wellies arguing with a concrete pump, and I learned something I should have known after twenty years: always ask where the water goes before you ask where the walls go.

This week's letter is about drainage, a subject nobody photographs and everybody pays for. I also found a lovely little book about gutters, which I'll tell you about at the end.

Until next Sunday,
Teresa

Below: my notes on slow proving, a loaf that finally worked, and the one thing I'd tell my younger self about humidity.

Back next Sunday,
Harriet

message.subject: Kitchen letters: the soup that saved my autumn
message.body:
Dear friends,

I hate to say it, but I have become a person who talks about soup. It started with a squash I couldn't bring myself to throw out, and now there's a pot on my stove from Sunday to Sunday.

This week's recipe is the one I keep making. I'll also tell you about the market stallholder who has refused to sell me anything but potatoes and what I think it means.

Until next Saturday,
Camille

Unsubscribe: https://camilleskitchen.example/stop

rationale: A personal-voice mailing to a list; no request.

message.subject: Churn model write-up
message.body:

Best,
Priya
Head of Analytics, Brightwell Logistics

message.body:
Daniel,

The revenue dashboard is showing zero for yesterday and the CFO is presenting it to the board at 3pm today. The nightly job seems to have run but the numbers are missing.

Can you look at it now and tell me what's going on? I need it fixed or a fallback before the CFO presents this afternoon.

Marta

rationale: A client needs an urgent fix before a 3pm presentation today.

message.subject: Your speaker slot
message.body:
Hi Daniel,

Helen

message.subject: Forecasting project: a quick chat?
message.body:
Hello Daniel,

Elena Rossi suggested I get in touch. We're looking at a demand-forecasting project for next year and she spoke very highly of you.

Would you be free for a 30-minute call sometime next week to talk it through? Happy to work around your diary.

Best regards,
Marcus Lee
Northbridge Energy

rationale: A polite request for a call that waits for an answer; 'sometime next week' proposes a window, not a lapse.

message.body:

No hurry, but a rough figure would help me with next year's budget.

Grazie mille,
Elena

message.subject: Noisy Estimates: confessions of a confidence interval
message.body:
Hello again,

I was asked at a dinner party last week what I do, and made the mistake of answering honestly. I now know that the phrase "ninety-five per cent confident" is a conversation killer.

This issue is my attempt to explain intervals to someone who stopped listening around the second sentence. There are three examples, one honest diagram and a confession about a spreadsheet I will not name.

Same time next week,
Hal

Unsubscribe: https://noisyestimates.example/leave

rationale: A personal-voice list mailing from one writer; no ask.
